children: Tech stocks rallied across the globe after Nvidia's market-beating earnings steadied investor sentiment following a leadership crisis at the chip company that compounded artificial-intelligence concerns.
Meanwhile, oil pulled back from highs earlier this week, while Treasurys were little moved ahead of the release of Federal Reserve meeting minutes Wednesday.

Nasdaq futures jumped 1%, while S&P futures traded 0.6% higher. Contracts tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.2%. Nvidia shares rose more than 3% premarket. The wider artificial-intelligence ecosystem gained too, with chip makers and cloud-computing stocks rising after Asian memory chip makers climbed overnight. South Korea's Kospi rose 2%, while the Nikkei Stock Average added 0.3%. Tech stocks rose in Europe, too, where ASML--the continent's most valuable stock--moved up close to 3% in early trade.

Nvidia's earnings arrived amid a wider selloff in AI-linked stocks since the beginning of October that preceded the departure of the chip company's chief executive, Jensen Huang. That departure prompted investor concerns that Nvidia would step back from its financing of other companies and reduce its spending on AI infrastructure.

Revenue beat expectations, while the company's newly appointed chairman sought to pour cold water on the possibility of Huang returning. Though a short-term boost for markets, the print isn't enough to answer broader concerns around the AI trade, UniCredit's Stefan Kolek said.

"While Nvidia once again delivered results and guidance above expectations, investors are still searching for evidence that the AI buildout can generate attractive and durable returns across the broader ecosystem," Kolek said.
Treasurys were little moved, with 10-year yields pulling back below 5.100%. Thirty-year yields traded around 5.440% and two-year yields were flat.

Benchmark oil prices pulled back as surplus expectations won out over investor concerns around renewed hostilities in the Middle East. Brent crude contracts fell 1.85% to trade around $91.50 a barrel. Metals prices fell sharply, with gold and copper both pulling back to multimonth lows. Gold futures slid around 2.4% to trade below $3,800 a troy ounce.

For the day ahead, Fed meeting minutes drive macro headlines. Investors will also keep an eye on the city of Shenzhen, China, where President Trump is set to meet Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin.

For the AI trade, markets watch for Anthropic's pricing of its highly anticipated initial-public offering, which is expected to be at the top end of the range. Cybersecurity group Palo Alto Networks reports earnings after the bell.
